text:
Ethan R.: SI flagged a blocker for a Redwood Dedicated on-prem install at AcmeCorp. Inference pods crash with GPU symbol errors during container startup.
Priya S.: can you paste the pod logs?
Ethan R.: SI paste: 
```
E031: failed to load /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.10.2: undefined symbol: __cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd
E031: TRT ERROR: Could not load CUDA runtime. Aborting.
container_linux.go:247: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:495: container init caused: rootfs_linux.go:54: mounting "/dev/nvidia0" to rootfs at "/dev/nvidia0" caused: no such device
```
Marco G.: looks like classic host driver / CUDA runtime mismatch + missing nvidia devices on the node. Are the nodes provisioning with GPU device plugin and correct driver?
Helen W.: SI says they used stock on-prem node image (vendor-provided) and didn't install our validated NVIDIA driver bundle. They assume container ships CUDA runtime so nothing needed on host. That's not correct for pinned kernels.
Priya S.: action items: 1) confirm host NVIDIA driver version and kernel match (run `nvidia-smi` on the node), 2) ensure NVIDIA device plugin is deployed, 3) install nvidia-container-toolkit or enable runtime.
Ethan R.: SI ran `nvidia-smi` and got: 
```
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Ensure that the latest driver is installed and running.
```
Marco G.: we should provide a short compatibility matrix and a validated host-image reference they can use. I can attach the matrix and our prebuilt validated AMI/OVA image tags.
Helen W.: also recommend a quick validation job they can run before deploying Marketplace: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-check
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia-a100
  containers:
  - name: nvidia-smi
    image: registry.redwood.ai/tools/nvidia-validator:1.0
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","nvidia-smi && python -c \"import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())\" "]
  restartPolicy: Never
```
Priya S.: also note: some environments lock kernel modules; if they use vendor-supplied images that omit drivers we provide a signed driver bundle they can install via their patch window. Provide checksum + install commands.
Ethan R.: SI asked if there is a CPU-only fallback for initial demo while infra patches drivers. Answer: yes, we have a CPU runtime image and a helm flag `resources.preferGpu=false` but that increases latency and cost. Good as stopgap.
Marco G.: raising to eng-runtime for a potential graceful failure mode that logs clearer onboarding instructions if CUDA missing. @Helen W. can you open a runtime ticket with logs and proposal?
Helen W.: opening RT ticket RT-8342: "Improve pod startup diagnostics for missing GPU drivers + add compatibility matrix link". CC @Marco G.
runtime-bot: RT-8342 created and assigned to eng-runtime-team. Initial ETA 3 days.
Priya S.: I'll send SI: 1) compatibility matrix + validated host image tags, 2) signed NVIDIA driver bundle + GPG fingerprint, 3) the `gpu-check` pod manifest, 4) CPU fallback helm flag and example values.
Ethan R.: SI will plan a maintenance window to install drivers tomorrow 02:00 UTC. They requested a short runbook snippet to present to their infra/SOC team showing steps, audit artifacts, and rollback.
Marco G.: I'll draft the runbook snippet: verify current driver (nvidia-smi), install driver package (dpkg/rpm commands), deploy nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet, deploy nvidia-container-toolkit, run `gpu-check`, then proceed with Marketplace install. Include commands and expected outputs.
Helen W.: add a note to partner-runbook: "If Dedicated on-prem deployment fails with CUDA/driver errors -> validate host driver first, provide signed driver bundle, or switch to CPU-only demo mode."
Ethan R.: SI thanked us. Scheduling the maintenance window and will update once drivers are patched. Thanks team. :pray:
